ftbpro_01m32hsca47t.title: Jose Mourinho’s Brutal Referee Takedown Gets Validation From La Liga
ftbpro_01m32hsca47t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas5:30 PM EDTJose Mourinho was furious with the refereeing decisions during the Madrid Derby.  / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesJose Mourinho’s vicious rant against the refereeing decisions that took place during Sunday’s Madrid derby has since earned some validation. La Liga’s Technical Committee of Referees (CTA) reportedly agree that Atlético Madrid’s Kang-In Lee should’ve been sent-off in the first half for a dangerous challenge that injured Real Madrid’s Federico Valverde.

Atlético Madrid defeated Real Madrid 2–1 in a hugely controversial derby on Sunday afternoon. Following the game, Real Madrid manager Mourinho slammed the refereeing decisions because he felt two particular actions were “clear red cards” and came prepared with photos of the actions as evidence.

One of those two actions was headlined by Lee, who caught Valverde with his studs right in the ankle during the dying minutes of a scoreless first half. It was an unquestionably-reckless action that injured Real Madrid’s captain and, incredibly, went unpunished, with neither match referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias nor VAR deeming it worthy of a red card.
CTA will offer a verdict on the controversial actions soon, but according to AS, the committee is already aware that Ortiz Arias made a number of mistakes, none bigger than letting Lee off the hook.

Kang-In Lee (left) should’ve been punished for this reckless challenge.  / Real MadridReal Madrid would’ve played with a man advantage for the entirety of the second half and, with the game still level at the break, the final outcome could’ve been much different.

Mourinho also asserted that Cristian Romero should’ve been sent off for catching Jude Bellingham on the knee with his studs earlier in the first half. Ortiz Arias initially booked the Englishman before VAR forced him to review the play for mistaken identity. The referee then switched his verdict, and Romero saw yellow—Mourinho wanted a different color. The review, though, was for mistaken identity, not to determine whether it was worthy of a red card. CTA reportedly excuse Ortiz Arias for his decision, given it was a chaotic action.

Finally, according to AS, CTA agree with the decision to send off Real Madrid center back Dean Huijsen for his foul on Atléti’s Giuliano Simeone, which resulted in a penalty. There was no attempt to play the ball, and he denied the Argentine from a clear goalscoring opportunity, which is why CTA agree that the double punishment (penalty and red card) was the correct decision in this instance.
Ultimately, Huijsen’s red card condemned Los Blancos, who backed their manager and released a statement with the title: “A dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby.”

Diego Simeone was quick to describe Mourinho’s unfiltered rant on Ortiz Arias, VAR and the Referee Appointment Committee, as “unacceptable,” accusing him of “crossing a line of respect.”
A day after the match, Atlético Madrid fired back at Mourinho and Los Blancos like they often do: with a series of social media posts.

Los Rojiblancos’ posted images of Mourinho holding up the photos he brought to his post-match press conference along with the title “Stop Referee Harassment Now.” Atléti poked fun at Mourinho’s bizarre antics by posting a video printing out their anti-referee harassment graphics and using a printer emoji as the caption.

This summer, Atlético Madrid went on a vicious social media tirade against Barcelona due to their pursuit of striker Julián Álvarez, posting a series of photoshopped images of Lamine Yamal, Raphinha and others wearing Atléti’s shirt. ftbpro_01m32s272k2z.title: USMNT Legend Tim Howard Explains Why America Is So Obsessed With Cavan Sullivan
ftbpro_01m32s272k2z.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely6:25 PM EDTTim Howard (left) is full onboard the “Cavan Sullivan” train. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Tim Howard); Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images (Cavan Sullivan)Another week, another breathtaking performance from Cavan Sullivan that makes American fans go wild.

The 16-year-old phenom took center stage once again in the Philadelphia Union’s unprecedented comeback on Saturday night, contributing a goal and assist in the eventual 4–3 win over Sporting Kansas City.

But these frenzied soccer fans aren’t just thrilled by the teenager’s mounting success. They’re obsessed with him. Former U.S. men’s national team legend Tim Howard thinks he knows why, because he feels it too. It requires flipping through the history books of American soccer.

“Going back a long time, I don’t know, decades and decades and decades and decades, we’ve had you [Landon Donovan], we’ve had Freddy Adu, we’ve had Christian Pulisic,” Howard said on his Unfiltered Soccer podcast. “Claudio Reyna was a young star, and he became great, but he wasn’t a phenom. He was very good in his teenage years.
“I look at Clint [Dempsey]. Clint is one of the greatest, if not the greatest, to ever do it, but he went to Furman. He was a late bloomer, and then he took the world by storm.”

For the former star goalkeeper, it all comes down to the numbers. In the history of men’s soccer, there have only been a few true prodigies of the game that have come up through the U.S. and utterly dominated the sport right from their early teenage years.

There’s Donovan, who debuted for the USMNT and attracted the attentions of the Bundesliga’s Bayer Leverkusen at 18 years old. There’s Adu, who stood as the youngest player to ever debut in Major League Soccer (14 years old) for 20 years, until Sullivan broke his record in 2024. The third and final, according to Howard, is Pulisic, a current USMNT legend that signed with Borussia Dortmund at just 16 years old. A prodigy is a rarity in the nation, unlike in other countries where soccer is the most popular sport on the men’s side and continually produces world-class talents.

“We’ve got three [prodigies],” Howard said, insinuating Sullivan would be the fourth in the men’s game. “Argentina has three every six months, so we are going to get excited about Cavan Sullivan. The whole country is going to get excited about him.”
He added: “People keep asking me this question for the last 20 years, ‘When is the U.S. going to produce a world-class talent?’ I’m not going to not get on board with this. I’m excited about it.”

Sullivan is unstoppable. /  Philadelphia Union/MLS/Getty ImagesSullivan ignited the Union’s second-half goalscoring frenzy on Saturday, which resulted in four unanswered goals and the continuation of the Union’s now 11-game unbeaten streak.

Just after the hour mark, the teenage midfielder beat four separate defenders in a lethal drive toward the center of the pitch, before pinging the ball to teammate Frankie Westfield on the opposite side. Westfield’s blast was deflected in by Union striker Bruno Damiani.
While the Union’s first goal put Sullivan’s technical savvy on full display, the second goal just four minutes later shined a light on his heightened soccer IQ.

Union midfielder Danley Jean Jacques darted from the flank toward the goal-line with the ball, and as soon as he did, Sullivan exploited the space in the center of the box, which had been left available by Milan Iloski making a run toward the goal mouth. Sullivan demanded the ball and received it from Jacques. Yet understanding that goalkeeper Stefan Cleveland had tracked his run and expected him to take a right-footed shot to the far right post, Sullivan quickly pivoted his stance, allowing him to instead make a unexpected, wide, left-footed finish into open netting.
CAVAN GETS HIS GOAL. 🇺🇸What a game in Kansas City. pic.twitter.com/rk0vVzVG2E

Sullivan isn’t just dominating a pitch of grown men. He’s shattering records. He’s now up to eight goals and 12 assists across all competitions thus far this season, including at least one goal contribution in the last eight-consecutive matches. With Saturday’s assist, he broke Alphonso Davies’s record for most assists in a regular season by a teenager (11), and he already broke Freddy Adu’s record for the most goal contributions by a 16-year-old (10) earlier this month.

He is simply unstoppable, and his breakout campaign has earned him a first-ever call up to the USMNT this fall. Sullivan will become the team’s youngest debutant since 16-year-old Adu took the pitch 20 years ago, should he appear in any one of the four international friendlies over the next two weeks.

Sullivan is not just matching the levels Donovan, Pulisic and Adu reached at his age, but actually exceeding him. Should he keep this pace, it is quite possible that Sullivan becomes the greatest talent in American soccer history.

fzhafkysws3g1ux8fnmoe3180.title: De la Fuente promises 'the best is yet to come' for Spain
fzhafkysws3g1ux8fnmoe3180.subtitle: Luis de la Fuente has penned a long-term contract extension to stay in charge of Spain, and he promised the best is still to come.
paragraphs: Spain boss Luis de la Fuente has vowed "the best is yet to come" from the reigning world and European champions.
De la Fuente has agreed a contract extension to stay in charge of Spain through to the end of Euro 2032.
Since De la Fuente replaced Luis Enrique in 2022, Spain have been dominant.
La Roja won Euro 2024 and then repeated the trick at this year's World Cup.
Spain are on a 38-game unbeaten run in competitive matches, which is a record for a European or South American team.
But De la Fuente insists Spain are not done yet.
"I only think about time and how fragile we are. Life has taught me to be very short-sighted," he said.

"My goal is to arrive in good shape for [Euro 2028]. But of course, I'm especially excited about reaching the 2030 World Cup, but also, now, the 2032 European Championship. We're going to try, with all our strength.
"The best is yet to come. The third star [World Cup crown] would be like something out of a movie."
Spain face England on Saturday before taking on Croatia and Czechia, in their opening Nations League games.

h7xm4yhya9qp1bvfflwf0ykr5.subtitle: Donyell Malen's withdrawal from the Netherlands squad may have concerned Roma supporters, but Xavi is confident he only has a minor injury.
paragraphs: The injury that caused Donyell Malen to withdraw from the Netherlands' squad is "not too bad", head coach Xavi said in a positive update on the Roma forward.
Malen has been in sensational form since swapping Aston Villa for the Italian capital in January.

Since making his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances in the competition, at least twice as many as any other player in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
He has helped the Giallorossi make a flying start to the new campaign under Gian Piero Gasperini, as they sit top of the table on goal difference heading into the international break.

Like Scudetto holders Inter, they opened 2026-27 with four straight victories, though they did let a 2-0 lead slip in Saturday's head-to-head clash between the top two, a game that saw Malen play the full 90 minutes.
Roma's supporters face a nervous wait regarding Malen's condition after he pulled out of Xavi's first Oranje squad, with reports suggesting it is a knee issue.
But Xavi does not believe it is a serious injury, having discussed the withdrawals of Malen and Justin Kluivert at a press conference on Monday.
"It's a pity, because Donyell is in splendid form, but it happened at the last moment, the same as Kluivert," Xavi said. "That's football, you have to adapt.
"I believe Donyell is okay, that it is not too bad. I don't know how long it will take for him to recover."
Malen has already scored six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, while over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player in the division and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes-per-goal rate in the Italian top flight.
Malen will sit out the Netherlands' Nations League meetings with Germany, Serbia (twice) and Greece, with Xavi's Oranje debut on Thursday pitting him against new Nationalelf boss Jurgen Klopp.

qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.title: Kolo Muani not facing spell out after hand surgery
qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.subtitle: Randal Kolo Muani has undergone surgery on a fractured finger on his right hand, but he will not miss any time for Juventus.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Randal Kolo Muani will remain available for selection after undergoing surgery on a fractured finger.
Kolo Muani played 89 minutes on Saturday as the Bianconeri returned to winning ways in Serie A, beating Atalanta 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium.
He played on despite sustaining an injury to his right hand, and though the issue required surgery, reports in Italy said he would return to training with Juve within a couple of days.
A statement released on Juve's website said: "During the first half of Sunday's match against Atalanta, Randal Kolo Muani sustained an injury to the fifth finger of his right hand.
"Tests carried out after the match revealed a fracture of the proximal phalanx, making osteosynthesis surgery necessary.
"The operation, performed this afternoon by Dr Loris Pegoli, was completely successful and the player will remain available for selection."
Kolo Muani has appeared in all six of the Bianconeri's matches in all competitions this season, starting five of those and recording one goal and two assists in 468 minutes.

He was not selected in Zinedine Zidane's first France squad ahead of their Nations League fixtures against Turkiye, Belgium and Italy, so will continue training with his club ahead of Juve facing Cagliari on October 11.

vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.title: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC: Dreyer strikes late to deny Messi and co.
vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.subtitle: Inter Miami's recent struggles continued as they played out yet another draw in MLS, losing more ground on the Eastern Conference leaders.
paragraphs: Anders Dreyer netted a late equaliser to earn San Diego FC a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami, who were held to a fourth straight stalemate despite Lionel Messi's free-kick.

Dreyer opened the scoring early on, but Miami turned the game on its head, with Messi and Luis Suarez both hitting the back of the net, only for San Diego's striker to complete his brace with eight minutes remaining at Nu Stadium.

San Diego's 12th-minute opener came out of nowhere as Jeppe Tverskov slotted a perfectly weighted throughball in behind for Dreyer, who charged in behind Miami's defense from the halfway line before dinking a lovely shot over Dayne St. Clair.
Twelve minutes later, Miami were back on level terms. Messi's free-kick looked to be more of a cross as it floated towards the far post, but it missed everyone in the middle and snuck in.

German Berterame's curler was cleared in front of the line by the retreating Ian Murphy, but San Diego could not clear their lines as Yannick Bright picked out Messi, whose first-time shot was kept out by CJ dos Santos.
Marcus Ingvartsen had a goal disallowed shortly after at the other end for an offside in the build-up, while Dos Santos punched away an awkward strike from Suarez.
But the Uruguayan soon got his goal in the 74th minute, lifting over Dos Santos from a tight angle to find the far corner.
Miami's lead only lasted eight minutes, though, with Dreyer again timing his run to perfection to meet a Tverskov pass, and a rooted St. Clair could not get a hand to it.

Messi had the chance to win it in stoppage time, bending a low shot through the crowded box, but Dos Santos got down to keep it out despite seeing it late, meaning Miami sit 11 points behind Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.
Messi makes more history despite Miami's frustrations
While Miami are unbeaten in their last five matches, they have drawn each of the last four, having held the lead in three of those.

But Messi has played his part in trying to get Miami back to winning ways, and netted his 101st goal for the Herons in total, while extending his lead in the Golden Boot race, as it was his 20th in MLS this season.
That means he is now just the second player in the league's history to score 20+ goals in three straight seasons, after Los Angeles FC's Denis Bouanga (2023-2025).
Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).
But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.
It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.title: Wirtz 'the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt' against Bournemouth, claims Carragher
vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.subtitle: Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact against Bournemouth, and Jamie Carragher has questioned his starting place going forward.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after the international break, claiming his performance against Bournemouth was the "poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt".
Liverpool edged to a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, giving Andoni Iraola a winning return to Vitality Stadium thanks to Alexander Isak's second-half goal.
Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983.
However, Wirtz came under fire for his performance on the south coast as he struggled to make an impact.
He finished the match with a team-low 70.3% passing accuracy (completing 26 of 37 passes), had 53 touches, and just two off-target shots, though he did create a joint-game-high three chances.
Only Ronald Araujo (24) lost possession more often than the German (16).
And Carragher was far from impressed by Wirtz's showing, claiming that Iraola needs to think about leaving him out of the side if they want to improve their results.
"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy; he keeps possession. There's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.
"But the reason I worry is: I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.
"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley, and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game, it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you.
"It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.
